practice_sources_note: At assignment the manifest mapped Lecture 57 (HIiybva-FN4) to Chapter 12. The author read its full publisher captions (16.32-1535.48 s), all three contact sheets, and native frames f0003, f0012, f0024 and f0043. Actual content is bond-market equilibrium, demand/supply shifts, Fisher effect, risk structure and ratings, not valuation or amortization worked practice. The lead independently verified and reassigned it to Chapter 13 in source-manifest.json during this draft. It supplies no substantive claim or exercise here. Detailed topic spans are in the private author report.
source_uncertainties: Durations use transcript.json: L39 1384 s, L40 2222 s and L41 1481 s; the manifest listed 1384, 2223 and 1482 s. All chapter timestamps lie inside both versions. The inspected/reassigned L57 has media duration 1545 s against manifest 1546 s, media SHA256 91a95492c1c2b51edff5f925743e37c6b7e2704f513449465891fe2895b36afc.

L39 f0003 explicitly uses P = Fr a + M v^n, then its alternative PVIFA/PVIF form identifies C = M. This bridge is stated before using C. Equality F = C = M = 100 occurs only in its numerical examples; face and redemption remain separate in the general model.

L39 f0009 has annual coupon 0.045/2, nominal annual yield 0.0453/2 and n = 30*2 = 60. The chapter distinguishes annual coupon quote r_ann, per-period coupon ratio r and cash c, and translates the slide's periodic yield i to the book's j explicitly.

L39 f0013 prints 99.5103 using rounded intermediate factors; recomputation without intermediate rounding gives 99.5104918351. L39 f0023 prints 101.765 after rounding factors; the unrounded result is 101.7658048197, or 101.77 to cents. The chapter states its final-only rounding convention.

L39 f0038 uses tilde-g = Fr/C for modified coupon; L40 f0064 and f0066 use g = Fr/C. The chapter defines g = tilde-g as the same coupon-per-redemption ratio and distinguishes it from earlier accumulation/payment-growth notation.

L40 f0027 and f0066 end the schedule at C after the final coupon, with redemption not deducted. The chapter explicitly fixes this intermediate state and then deducts redemption to reach zero. It does not describe the post-all-cash-flows balance as C.

L40 speech around 796-804 s suggests effective interest rises in the premium example; f0027 shows it falling from 20.56 to 20.10 as book value falls. The chapter follows the table and the fixed-yield equation. f0057 shows the opposite trend for a discount. Monetary discount 27.09 is not treated as a percentage.

L40 mentions accounting and taxation and calls the method common; L41 gives an accounting description of book value. No accounting-law or tax-law source was checked, so the chapter confines book value to the stated mathematical fixed-yield model and makes no GAAP, tax or prevalence claim.

L41 f0012 states annual coupon 5%, nominal semiannual yield 4%, maturity after six coupons and first call after coupon four. f0013/f0017 print 1000*0.02 = 25, an arithmetic and rate-label error; c = 1000*0.025 = 25 is used consistently. The same printed note labels the four-period call calculation maturity; the chapter retains first call = 4 and maturity = 6.

L41 f0018 prose mentions call periods only through 20 while the displayed second branch and f0026 full table extend through 30. The chapter uses the displayed piecewise contract and all sixteen periods 15-30, which the computation verifies; the minimum is at 20.

L41 f0009 and speech 244.96-276.24 discuss earliest or maturity call under unchanged yield and a constant redemption amount. The chapter proves the candidate-price comparison under those hypotheses and treats the minimum as a conservative contractual yield criterion, not a general option-price or issuer-exercise theorem.

L41 zero-coupon labels may suggest zero interest; the chapter distinguishes a zero coupon from the positive yield computed in f0033. It uses an explicitly annual period for the 520-to-1000 five-year example. The consol historical anecdote and claims about rarity are not used as independently verified findings.

L41 f0044 and speech contrast market value with book value but can be read as saying book value never changes and always ends at face. f0047 itself shows an amortizing book value. The chapter says a fixed-date market-yield change does not change the chosen schedule, while time changes its book value; the terminal intermediate amount is redemption C, which equals face only if the contract says so.

No lecture section among 39-41 develops clean/dirty pricing or a day-count convention. Those are not invented as lecture material; the coupon-date boundary is explicit and independently corroborated only as an Exam FM syllabus scope statement.

All assigned captions were read sequentially in full, and all thirteen contact sheets were scanned before selecting native frames. None of the relied-on formulas or table entries remained unreadable. The instructor/book reference names mentioned in recordings are not used as inaccessible textbook citations.
